title: Apple Pie
subtitle: a deep-filled double-crust pie with spiced apple
excerpt: A double-crust pie filled with cinnamon-spiced apples that stay in pieces rather than collapsing to mush. The pastry lid must be vented to let steam escape. Serve warm with cream, custard, or vanilla ice cream.
sourceNotes: A British and American classic. This version uses a traditional shortcrust and Bramley apples for cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked. Bake from frozen at 200C adding 15 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble and refrigerate unbaked for up to 24 hours.

content.text: Use a mix of cooking apples and eating apples if you can. Bramley apples break down and give a saucy base while firmer eating apples keep some texture. Toss the sliced apples with sugar and cinnamon and leave for 20 minutes -- the juice that releases will concentrate during baking.

items.prepNote: 80g for the filling, 20g for the pastry
yolk for pastry, beaten white for brushing the lid
juice and zest -- to stop apples browning and brighten flavour
use 1 tbsp cold water to seal the pastry edge

content.text: Make the pastry: rub the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add the sugar, egg yolk, and cold water. Bring together into a disc. Chill for 30 minutes.
Peel, core, and slice the apples (about 1kg total -- 4 to 5 large apples). Toss with the sugar, cinnamon, lemon zest, and juice. Leave while the pastry chills.
Heat the oven to 200C. Divide the pastry into two pieces. Roll one out and line a 23cm pie dish. Drain excess juice from the apples and pile into the dish, mounding slightly.

Roll the second pastry piece for the lid. Brush the rim with cold water. Lay the lid over and press to seal. Trim the edges and crimp. Cut a few slits in the top for steam. Brush with beaten egg white and scatter with a little sugar.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden. Rest for 20 minutes before serving -- the filling needs to settle.

items.cause: Too much juice from the apples, or the dish was not preheated.
items.fix: Drain the macerated apples before filling. Place the pie dish on a hot baking sheet in the oven to help the base cook through.

items.symptom: Pastry lid collapses into the apples
items.cause: Not enough apples to support the lid.
items.fix: Mound the filling generously -- it will sink as it cooks. You can also add a ceramic pie bird in the centre.

content.text: Apple pie is claimed by both Britain and America, with good reason -- both have long traditions of double-crust fruit pies made with tart cooking apples. The British version tends to use Bramley apples and a lid only, while the American version often has a full double crust. Both are best in autumn when apples are at their peak.
